import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The γ–θ conjecture (eternal domination)

The *eternal domination game* (one-guard-moves model) is played on a finite graph $G$ by a
defender and an attacker. The defender first places guards on a dominating set $D_1$ (at most one
guard per vertex). Then, at each turn, the attacker attacks a vertex $r_i$. If $r_i$ is unoccupied,
the defender must move exactly one guard from a vertex of $D_i$ adjacent to $r_i$ onto $r_i$; the
new configuration $D_{i+1}$ must again be a dominating set. The defender wins if they can defend
every infinite sequence of attacks. A set $D$ is an *eternal dominating set* if the defender wins
when starting from $D$, and the *eternal domination number* $\gamma_\infty(G)$ is the minimum size
of an eternal dominating set. This is the model of Burger et al.; it is not the *m-eternal*
(all-guards-move) variant.

The *clique covering number* $\theta(G)$ is the minimum number of cliques partitioning the
vertices of $G$; equivalently, it is the chromatic number of the complement of $G$.

Since $\gamma(G) \leq \gamma_\infty(G) \leq \theta(G)$, where $\gamma$ is the domination number,
the γ–θ conjecture ($\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G)$ if and only if $\gamma(G) = \theta(G)$, for
every graph $G$) fails exactly when there is a graph $G$ with
$\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G) < \theta(G)$. Whether such a graph exists is Question 1 of
Klostermeyer and Mynhardt [KM15a], listed as one of the main open questions in the survey
[KM15b]. Such a graph must contain a triangle and have maximum degree at least four [KM15a].

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Eternal dominating set*, § Open questions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal_dominating_set%23Open_questions)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KM15a] W. F. Klostermeyer and C. M. Mynhardt, *Domination, Eternal Domination, and Clique
  Covering*, Discuss. Math. Graph Theory 35 (2015), 283–300.
  [arXiv:1407.5235](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5235)
- [KM15b] W. F. Klostermeyer and C. M. Mynhardt, *Protecting a graph with mobile guards*,
  Appl. Anal. Discrete Math. 10 (2016), 1–29. [arXiv:1407.5228](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5228)
-/
namespace Conjecture
open SimpleGraph
variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

blocks.docstring:
A family `𝓕` of vertex sets of `G` is an *eternal dominating family* (one-guard-moves model)
if every member of `𝓕` is a dominating set and, for every configuration `D ∈ 𝓕` and every
attack at an unoccupied vertex `r ∉ D`, some guard standing on a vertex `v ∈ D` adjacent to `r`
can move to `r` so that the new configuration `(D \ {v}) ∪ {r}` again lies in `𝓕`.

Attacks at occupied vertices need no response, so they are not modelled.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.IsDominating` / `SimpleGraph.dominationNumber` (FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Domination) — static domination only; reused as a component.
justification.name: Conjecture.IsEternalDominatingFamily
justification.why_needed: No notion of eternal domination (mobile guards / one-guard-moves game) exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib. A family 𝓕 of dominating finsets closed under the response rule: for D ∈ 𝓕 and r ∉ D there is v ∈ D adjacent to r with `insert r (D.erase v) ∈ 𝓕`.

blocks.name: IsEternalDominatingFamily
blocks.text:
/-- A family `𝓕` of vertex sets of `G` is an *eternal dominating family* (one-guard-moves model)
if every member of `𝓕` is a dominating set and, for every configuration `D ∈ 𝓕` and every
attack at an unoccupied vertex `r ∉ D`, some guard standing on a vertex `v ∈ D` adjacent to `r`
can move to `r` so that the new configuration `(D \ {v}) ∪ {r}` again lies in `𝓕`.

Attacks at occupied vertices need no response, so they are not modelled. -/
def IsEternalDominatingFamily (G : SimpleGraph V) (𝓕 : Set (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  (∀ D ∈ 𝓕, G.IsDominating (D : Set V)) ∧
    ∀ D ∈ 𝓕, ∀ r ∉ D, ∃ v ∈ D, G.Adj v r ∧ insert r (D.erase v) ∈ 𝓕

blocks.code:
def IsEternalDominating (G : SimpleGraph V) (D : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝓕, IsEternalDominatingFamily G 𝓕 ∧ D ∈ 𝓕
blocks.docstring:
A finite set `D` of vertices of `G` is an *eternal dominating set* if placing one guard on
each vertex of `D` lets the defender defend every infinite sequence of attacks, moving one guard
per attack and keeping the guards on a dominating set. Equivalently, `D` belongs to some eternal
dominating family: the defender wins by always staying inside that family (the eternal domination
game is a safety game, so positional strategies suffice).

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.IsDominating`, `SimpleGraph.IsTotalDominating`, `IsWellTotallyDominated` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib — none model mobile guards.
justification.name: Conjecture.IsEternalDominating
justification.why_needed: An eternal dominating set is a configuration from which the defender wins the eternal domination game; encoded as membership in some eternal dominating family.

blocks.name: IsEternalDominating
blocks.text:
/-- A finite set `D` of vertices of `G` is an *eternal dominating set* if placing one guard on
each vertex of `D` lets the defender defend every infinite sequence of attacks, moving one guard
per attack and keeping the guards on a dominating set. Equivalently, `D` belongs to some eternal
dominating family: the defender wins by always staying inside that family (the eternal domination
game is a safety game, so positional strategies suffice). -/
def IsEternalDominating (G : SimpleGraph V) (D : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝓕, IsEternalDominatingFamily G 𝓕 ∧ D ∈ 𝓕

blocks.code:
noncomputable def eternalDominationNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ D : Finset V, IsEternalDominating G D ∧ D.card = n}
blocks.docstring:
The *eternal domination number* $\gamma_\infty(G)$ of `G` is the least size of an eternal
dominating set of `G` (in the one-guard-moves model). For a finite graph this is a true minimum,
since the whole vertex set is an eternal dominating set.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.dominationNumber` (same sInf pattern, reused for γ) and `SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber` (used for θ via the complement).
justification.name: Conjecture.eternalDominationNumber
justification.why_needed: γ∞(G), the minimum size of an eternal dominating set, is one of the three invariants in the statement and is absent from Mathlib and the repo.

blocks.name: eternalDominationNumber
blocks.text:
/-- The *eternal domination number* $\gamma_\infty(G)$ of `G` is the least size of an eternal
dominating set of `G` (in the one-guard-moves model). For a finite graph this is a true minimum,
since the whole vertex set is an eternal dominating set. -/
noncomputable def eternalDominationNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ D : Finset V, IsEternalDominating G D ∧ D.card = n}

/-- The domination number $\gamma(G)$. -/
local notation "γ(" G ")" => dominationNumber G

/-- The eternal domination number $\gamma_\infty(G)$ (one-guard-moves model). -/
local notation "γ∞(" G ")" => eternalDominationNumber G

/-- The clique covering number $\theta(G)$: the least number of cliques partitioning the vertex
set of `G`, which is the chromatic number of the complement of `G`. -/
local notation "θ(" G ")" => chromaticNumber Gᶜ

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsEternalDominating.isDominating {G : SimpleGraph V} {D : Finset V}
    (hD : IsEternalDominating G D) : G.IsDominating (D : Set V) :=
  let ⟨_, h𝓕, hD⟩ := hD
  h𝓕.1 D hD

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isEternalDominating_singleton_top (v : V) :
    IsEternalDominating (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) {v} := by
  refine ⟨Set.range fun w : V => ({w} : Finset V), ⟨?_, ?_⟩, v, rfl⟩
  · rintro D ⟨w, rfl⟩ u
    by_cases huw : u = w
    · exact Or.inl (by simp [huw])
    · exact Or.inr ⟨w, by simp, huw⟩
  · rintro D ⟨w, rfl⟩ r hr
    have hwr : w ≠ r := fun h => hr (by simp [h])
    exact ⟨w, by simp, hwr, r, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isEternalDominating_pathGraph_three :
    ¬ IsEternalDominating (pathGraph 3) {1} := by
  rintro ⟨𝓕, h𝓕, hD⟩
  obtain ⟨v, hv, -, hmem⟩ := h𝓕.2 _ hD 0 (by decide)
  have hv' : v = 1 := by simpa using hv
  subst hv'
  rw [show insert (0 : Fin 3) (({1} : Finset (Fin 3)).erase 1) = {0} by decide] at hmem
  simpa [pathGraph_adj] using h𝓕.1 {0} hmem 2
blocks.docstring:
The centre of the path on three vertices is a dominating set but not an eternal dominating
set: after the guard moves to defend an attack at an end vertex, the other end vertex is no
longer dominated.

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem eternalDominationNumber_top [Nonempty V] : γ∞((⊤ : SimpleGraph V)) = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨v⟩ := ‹Nonempty V›
  refine le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le ⟨{v}, isEternalDominating_singleton_top v, by simp⟩) ?_
  refine le_csInf ⟨1, {v}, isEternalDominating_singleton_top v, by simp⟩ ?_
  rintro n ⟨D, hD, rfl⟩
  rw [Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero, Ne, Finset.card_eq_zero]
  rintro rfl
  simpa using hD.isDominating v

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isEternalDominating_univ (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsEternalDominating G Finset.univ := by
  refine ⟨{Finset.univ}, ⟨fun D hD v => Or.inl ?_, fun D hD r hr => ?_⟩, rfl⟩
  · rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hD]
    exact Finset.mem_univ v
  · rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hD] at hr
    exact (hr (Finset.mem_univ r)).elim

blocks.docstring:
**γ–θ conjecture.** Does there exist a (finite simple) graph $G$ whose domination number
$\gamma(G)$, eternal domination number $\gamma_\infty(G)$ (one-guard-moves model) and clique
covering number $\theta(G)$ satisfy $\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G) < \theta(G)$?

Here $\theta(G)$ is expressed as the chromatic number of the complement of $G$, to which it is
equal. Since $\gamma(G) \leq \gamma_\infty(G) \leq \theta(G)$ for every graph, such a graph exists
if and only if the γ–θ conjecture, "$\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G)$ if and only if
$\gamma(G) = \theta(G)$ for every graph $G$", is false. This is Question 1 of [KM15a].

claims.decomposer_note: A single yes/no existence question over finite simple graphs (answer unknown, so an answer(sorry)-style Prop); it is equivalent to the negation of the article's 'γ–θ conjecture' (∀ G, γ(G)=γ∞(G) ↔ γ(G)=θ(G)) via the chain γ ≤ γ∞ ≤ θ, and γ∞ must be the one-guard-moves eternal domination number (Question 1 of Klostermeyer–Mynhardt, arXiv:1407.5235), not the m-eternal variant; the 'must contain a triangle / Δ ≥ 4' facts are known theorems, not posed questions.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ finite simple graph G, γ(G) = γ∞(G) ∧ γ(G) < θ(G)` (some use γ∞ < θ, equivalent under the first conjunct), with γ = repo `SimpleGraph.dominationNumber`, θ = Mathlib `Gᶜ.chromaticNumber` (exactly the paper's definition θ(G)=χ(Ḡ); c05's bespoke partition-based clique cover number is also correct), and a bespoke one-guard-moves eternal domination number. Two encodings of the infinite game appear: invariant/closed family of configurations (c01,c03,c04,c05,c07,c08) and history-indexed strategy functions (c02,c06); both are correct encodings of 'defender wins the safety game' against an adaptive attacker and agree with Klostermeyer–Mynhardt's definition (D_{i+1} = (D_i − {v}) ∪ {r_i}, v ∈ D_i adjacent to r_i, all D_i dominating; attacks at occupied vertices WLOG ignored). Boundary: n = 0 gives 0 = 0 < 0, false, so no spurious witness. I chose c04 as the base for its clean definitions (no unnecessary Fintype on defs), local notation γ( )/γ∞( )/θ( ), API lemma γ ≤ γ∞, and thorough docstring/references, and added the pathGraph-3 and complete-graph tests from c07/c01 (adapted to c04's definitions). Edits: moved `eternalDominationNumber_top` above `variable [Fintype V]` to avoid an unused-section-variable linter warning.

context:
In graph theory, an eternal dominating set for a graph G = (V, E) is a subset D of V such that D is a dominating set on which mobile guards are initially located (at most one guard may be located on any vertex). The set D must be such that for any infinite sequence of attacks occurring sequentially at vertices, the set D can be modified by moving a guard from an adjacent vertex to the attacked vertex, provided the attacked vertex has no guard on it at the time it is attacked. The configuration of guards after each attack must induce a dominating set. The eternal domination number, γ∞(G),  is the minimum number of vertices possible in the initial set D. For example, the eternal domination number of the cycle on five vertices is three.
The eternal dominating set problem, also known as the eternal domination problem and the eternal security problem, can also be interpreted as a combinatorial game played between two players that alternate turns: a defender, who chooses the initial dominating set D and the guard to send to each attack that occurs at a vertex without a guard; and an attacker, who chooses the vertex to be attacked on their turn. The attacker wins the game if they can ever choose a vertex to be attacked such that there is no guard on that vertex or a neighboring vertex; the defender wins otherwise. In other words, the attacker wins the game if they can ever attack a vertex such that the attack cannot be defended.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The γ–θ conjecture (eternal domination)

The *eternal domination game* (one-guard-moves model) is played on a finite graph $G$ by a
defender and an attacker. The defender first places guards on a dominating set $D_1$ (at most one
guard per vertex). Then, at each turn, the attacker attacks a vertex $r_i$. If $r_i$ is unoccupied,
the defender must move exactly one guard from a vertex of $D_i$ adjacent to $r_i$ onto $r_i$; the
new configuration $D_{i+1}$ must again be a dominating set. The defender wins if they can defend
every infinite sequence of attacks. A set $D$ is an *eternal dominating set* if the defender wins
when starting from $D$, and the *eternal domination number* $\gamma_\infty(G)$ is the minimum size
of an eternal dominating set. This is the model of Burger et al.; it is not the *m-eternal*
(all-guards-move) variant.

The *clique covering number* $\theta(G)$ is the minimum number of cliques partitioning the
vertices of $G$; equivalently, it is the chromatic number of the complement of $G$.

Since $\gamma(G) \leq \gamma_\infty(G) \leq \theta(G)$, where $\gamma$ is the domination number,
the γ–θ conjecture ($\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G)$ if and only if $\gamma(G) = \theta(G)$, for
every graph $G$) fails exactly when there is a graph $G$ with
$\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G) < \theta(G)$. Whether such a graph exists is Question 1 of
Klostermeyer and Mynhardt [KM15a], listed as one of the main open questions in the survey
[KM15b]. Such a graph must contain a triangle and have maximum degree at least four [KM15a].

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Eternal dominating set*, § Open questions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal_dominating_set%23Open_questions)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KM15a] W. F. Klostermeyer and C. M. Mynhardt, *Domination, Eternal Domination, and Clique
  Covering*, Discuss. Math. Graph Theory 35 (2015), 283–300.
  [arXiv:1407.5235](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5235)
- [KM15b] W. F. Klostermeyer and C. M. Mynhardt, *Protecting a graph with mobile guards*,
  Appl. Anal. Discrete Math. 10 (2016), 1–29. [arXiv:1407.5228](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5228)
-/

namespace Conjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

/-- A family `𝓕` of vertex sets of `G` is an *eternal dominating family* (one-guard-moves model)
if every member of `𝓕` is a dominating set and, for every configuration `D ∈ 𝓕` and every
attack at an unoccupied vertex `r ∉ D`, some guard standing on a vertex `v ∈ D` adjacent to `r`
can move to `r` so that the new configuration `(D \ {v}) ∪ {r}` again lies in `𝓕`.

Attacks at occupied vertices need no response, so they are not modelled. -/
def IsEternalDominatingFamily (G : SimpleGraph V) (𝓕 : Set (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  (∀ D ∈ 𝓕, G.IsDominating (D : Set V)) ∧
    ∀ D ∈ 𝓕, ∀ r ∉ D, ∃ v ∈ D, G.Adj v r ∧ insert r (D.erase v) ∈ 𝓕

/-- A finite set `D` of vertices of `G` is an *eternal dominating set* if placing one guard on
each vertex of `D` lets the defender defend every infinite sequence of attacks, moving one guard
per attack and keeping the guards on a dominating set. Equivalently, `D` belongs to some eternal
dominating family: the defender wins by always staying inside that family (the eternal domination
game is a safety game, so positional strategies suffice). -/
def IsEternalDominating (G : SimpleGraph V) (D : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝓕, IsEternalDominatingFamily G 𝓕 ∧ D ∈ 𝓕

/-- The *eternal domination number* $\gamma_\infty(G)$ of `G` is the least size of an eternal
dominating set of `G` (in the one-guard-moves model). For a finite graph this is a true minimum,
since the whole vertex set is an eternal dominating set. -/
noncomputable def eternalDominationNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ D : Finset V, IsEternalDominating G D ∧ D.card = n}

/-- The domination number $\gamma(G)$. -/
local notation "γ(" G ")" => dominationNumber G

/-- The eternal domination number $\gamma_\infty(G)$ (one-guard-moves model). -/
local notation "γ∞(" G ")" => eternalDominationNumber G

/-- The clique covering number $\theta(G)$: the least number of cliques partitioning the vertex
set of `G`, which is the chromatic number of the complement of `G`. -/
local notation "θ(" G ")" => chromaticNumber Gᶜ

/-- Every eternal dominating set is a dominating set. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsEternalDominating.isDominating {G : SimpleGraph V} {D : Finset V}
    (hD : IsEternalDominating G D) : G.IsDominating (D : Set V) :=
  let ⟨_, h𝓕, hD⟩ := hD
  h𝓕.1 D hD

/-- In a complete graph with at least one vertex, a single guard suffices: it simply moves to
every attacked vertex. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isEternalDominating_singleton_top (v : V) :
    IsEternalDominating (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) {v} := by
  refine ⟨Set.range fun w : V => ({w} : Finset V), ⟨?_, ?_⟩, v, rfl⟩
  · rintro D ⟨w, rfl⟩ u
    by_cases huw : u = w
    · exact Or.inl (by simp [huw])
    · exact Or.inr ⟨w, by simp, huw⟩
  · rintro D ⟨w, rfl⟩ r hr
    have hwr : w ≠ r := fun h => hr (by simp [h])
    exact ⟨w, by simp, hwr, r, by simp⟩

/-- The empty set is not an eternal dominating set of a graph with a vertex. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isEternalDominating_empty (G : SimpleGraph V) [Nonempty V] :
    ¬ IsEternalDominating G ∅ := by
  rintro ⟨𝓕, h𝓕, h⟩
  obtain ⟨v⟩ := ‹Nonempty V›
  simpa using h𝓕.1 ∅ h v

/-- The centre of the path on three vertices is a dominating set but not an eternal dominating
set: after the guard moves to defend an attack at an end vertex, the other end vertex is no
longer dominated. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isEternalDominating_pathGraph_three :
    ¬ IsEternalDominating (pathGraph 3) {1} := by
  rintro ⟨𝓕, h𝓕, hD⟩
  obtain ⟨v, hv, -, hmem⟩ := h𝓕.2 _ hD 0 (by decide)
  have hv' : v = 1 := by simpa using hv
  subst hv'
  rw [show insert (0 : Fin 3) (({1} : Finset (Fin 3)).erase 1) = {0} by decide] at hmem
  simpa [pathGraph_adj] using h𝓕.1 {0} hmem 2

/-- The eternal domination number of a nonempty complete graph is `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem eternalDominationNumber_top [Nonempty V] : γ∞((⊤ : SimpleGraph V)) = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨v⟩ := ‹Nonempty V›
  refine le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le ⟨{v}, isEternalDominating_singleton_top v, by simp⟩) ?_
  refine le_csInf ⟨1, {v}, isEternalDominating_singleton_top v, by simp⟩ ?_
  rintro n ⟨D, hD, rfl⟩
  rw [Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero, Ne, Finset.card_eq_zero]
  rintro rfl
  simpa using hD.isDominating v

variable [Fintype V]

/-- The whole vertex set is an eternal dominating set: no vertex is ever unoccupied. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isEternalDominating_univ (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsEternalDominating G Finset.univ := by
  refine ⟨{Finset.univ}, ⟨fun D hD v => Or.inl ?_, fun D hD r hr => ?_⟩, rfl⟩
  · rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hD]
    exact Finset.mem_univ v
  · rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hD] at hr
    exact (hr (Finset.mem_univ r)).elim

/-- The eternal domination number is at most the number of vertices. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem eternalDominationNumber_le_card (G : SimpleGraph V) : γ∞(G) ≤ Fintype.card V :=
  Nat.sInf_le ⟨Finset.univ, isEternalDominating_univ G, Finset.card_univ⟩

/-- Every eternal dominating set is a dominating set, so $\gamma(G) \leq \gamma_\infty(G)$. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem dominationNumber_le_eternalDominationNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) : γ(G) ≤ γ∞(G) := by
  refine csInf_le_csInf' ⟨_, Finset.univ, isEternalDominating_univ G, rfl⟩ ?_
  rintro n ⟨D, hD, rfl⟩
  exact ⟨D, hD.isDominating, rfl⟩

/-- **γ–θ conjecture.** Does there exist a (finite simple) graph $G$ whose domination number
$\gamma(G)$, eternal domination number $\gamma_\infty(G)$ (one-guard-moves model) and clique
covering number $\theta(G)$ satisfy $\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G) < \theta(G)$?

Here $\theta(G)$ is expressed as the chromatic number of the complement of $G$, to which it is
equal. Since $\gamma(G) \leq \gamma_\infty(G) \leq \theta(G)$ for every graph, such a graph exists
if and only if the γ–θ conjecture, "$\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G)$ if and only if
$\gamma(G) = \theta(G)$ for every graph $G$", is false. This is Question 1 of [KM15a]. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 91]
theorem conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), γ(G) = γ∞(G) ∧ (γ(G) : ℕ∞) < θ(G) := by
  sorry

end Conjecture

items: Graphs range over all finite simple graphs, encoded as `SimpleGraph (Fin n)` for some `n : ℕ` (every finite graph is isomorphic to one on `Fin n`; all three invariants are isomorphism invariants). `n = 0` gives γ = γ∞ = θ = 0, so it is not a degenerate witness.

The eternal domination number is the one-guard-moves model (Burger et al.; Klostermeyer–Mynhardt), not the m-eternal (all-guards-move) variant, as required by the decomposition notes. In the model, after an attack at an unoccupied vertex r exactly one guard moves from a vertex v ∈ D adjacent to r onto r; the new configuration is `insert r (D.erase v)`; every configuration must be a dominating set.

The infinite adaptive game ('defender can defend any infinite sequence of attacks') is encoded via closed families: `D` is eternal dominating iff it belongs to a set 𝓕 of dominating sets such that every attack at an unoccupied vertex of any member of 𝓕 can be answered inside 𝓕. This is the standard greatest-fixed-point characterization of winning positions in a safety game (the set of all winning configurations is such a family; any such family yields a positional winning strategy). The naive `∀ attack sequence, ∃ response sequence` formulation was deliberately avoided because it would give the defender clairvoyance.
Attacks at occupied vertices are not modelled since they require no response (the sources assume WLOG r_i ∉ D_i).

Clique covering number θ(G) is taken as the chromatic number of the complement graph (Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber`, valued in ℕ∞), exactly as the cited paper defines it ('θ(G) equals the chromatic number χ(Ḡ)'). Since γ : ℕ, the strict inequality is stated after casting γ to ℕ∞.

`answer(True)` means such a graph exists, i.e. the γ–θ conjecture (∀ G, γ = γ∞ ↔ γ = θ) is false; `answer(False)` means it is true. The equivalence relies on the known chain γ ≤ γ∞ ≤ θ, recorded in the docstring; the γ ≤ γ∞ half is proved as an API lemma in the file.

`eternalDominationNumber` is defined for an arbitrary vertex type (like the repo's `dominationNumber`), as `sInf` of the sizes of eternal dominating sets; for finite `V` the set is nonempty (`Finset.univ` is eternal dominating, proved in the file), so it is a genuine minimum. The conjecture only uses finite vertex types.
AMS tags 5 (combinatorics) and 91 (game theory, cf. 91A43 games involving graphs); the source paper's own classification is 05C69.
